html: The Djugun, shown on the map as Jukun from 1600 to 1815, were a small Aboriginal Australian people of the coast just north of present-day Broome in the Kimberley. Their neighbours were the Ngumbarl, the Jabirr Jabirr and the Nimanburu to the north and the Karajarri to the south. Their language belonged to the Nyulnyulan family and is no longer spoken. From the 1880s Broome grew as the centre of the pearling industry, and the Djugun were among the first people of the area to feel its weight.
